interpretation: Axes describe audited dispatch domains, not a Cartesian product of supported capabilities. Native source presence, Python wrapper parity, and a test path are not endpoint or numerical acceptance. Runtime capability and independent exact-head evidence remain separate authorities. Source SHA pins the pre-cutover baseline; follow-up migrations do not silently rewrite it.

remaining_python_runtime: Per-item stationary source preparation and force assembly; qualified native DF-PBE/PBE0 takes the separate native row.
Tile/task, AO/Becke/XC/correction scheduling and complete force publication remain Python-owned. Native source bridges are not native force endpoints.
Method-specific nuclear RHS, response schedule, seven stationary HVP sources, grid response and Cartesian-column publication remain Python-owned. A native source/action is not a complete SDK HVP.

Eligible CPU host solves and recycled inner solves use shared native GMRES. Independent sequential CPU RHS schedules stream through the native bound response owner with prefix admission and synchronous publication. Eligible CPU FP64 recycle-vector retention, projection and old-first MGS replacement use the native owner without normal per-solve vector publication. Python retains method-specific operator callbacks, recycled/block schedules, value-only RHS-rank SVD, explicit seed/transport/foreign compatibility and XC tiles; complete native molecular Hessian/HVP assembly and cross-backend resource authority remain outstanding.

Blocked solves, explicit/resident vector engines, device providers, general preconditioners, solution consumers and zero-dimensional problems retain their existing controllers. Foreign RHS dtypes/negative or unaligned strides preserve their existing sequential schedule. Missing optional native protocols are explicit compatibility; native/load failures never retry Python arithmetic. Do not replace distinct CPHF, Lambda or CC equations with one symmetric operator.

CPU/CUDA HF/KS compact expanded-contraction topology counts use an additive native query on the selected library, sharing AO representation arithmetic with normalized native systems. Python still expands basis records and owns mathematical provenance, capability checks and ECP descriptors. Missing-symbol and library-free shape plans retain explicit portable arithmetic. The query performs no backend/device discovery. Native refusal does not retry portable sizing; shape counts are not full allocation/provider/lease authority.

CPU HF and CPU/CUDA KS host per-item/retained/serialized-fleet capacities share native CLI/C++ owners when their additive queries are discovered. KS passes its explicit CPU transient floor or CUDA retained consumer allowances to the native fleet peak check without transferring consumer eligibility/admission policy; the ordinary native CLI excludes Python snapshot/force consumers. HF/KS CPU/CUDA ECP workspace sizing uses the discovered native two-grid query, independently of the enclosing inventory ABI. D3(BJ) retained plan/execution, table and workspace capacities query the same native layout used by D3Plan::prepare, including a shape-only CUDA selector. Library-free dry runs and old libraries retain explicit portable metadata sizing, including per-item-only ABI fallback. Python retains consumer allowance/eligibility policy and method/provider inventory construction.

CUDA KS device per-item setup, retained arena/provider sums, serialized rebuild excess and minimum/cached stationary declared-device peaks use discovered native fleet composition, shared with native CLI ordinary-energy dry runs. Python obtains the existing native allocator leaves, marshals topology/consumer inventories and publishes resource metadata; missing-symbol libraries retain explicit legacy per-item composition. Native refusal or inconsistent publication never retries Python sizing. This does not transfer consumer admission or establish complete physical/provider/lease/RSS authority.

Discovered native global composition owns sparse lifetime peaks, exact effective caps, supported-candidate ranking and fixed-selection declared-capacity admission, shared with the CLI. Selected device-ledger binding also derives numeric limits and allowance-separated declared peaks natively, without CUDA operations. Python still constructs method/provider inventories and supported alternatives; ResourcePlan independently validates and serializes derived metadata. Library-free/old-library planning and ledger compatibility, compiler planning and generic session/retry lifecycle remain portable. Native allocation receipts do not prove complete planner coverage or endpoint/RSS bounds; MINAO numeric capacity is already a native additive query.

With the additive prepared-resource ABI, Calculation and PreparedBatch pass the selected inventory once and native owners retain admission across construction, execution, independent ports and destruction. Python reads snapshots without owning those binding scopes; absent-symbol libraries alone retain the explicit older observation adapter. Numeric-cap strict-FP64 all-electron s/p PBE/PBE0 KS has native mandatory fleet promises and unpromised optional XC admission; unsupported controls and capacity misses retain bounded incumbent admission. Selected external inventories keep dense/single-tile behavior. This does not transfer all Python inventory selection, admit public CUDA DF KS forces, or establish complete opaque provider/RSS accounting.

Admitted complete named KS/D3 programs query the native per-item correction inventory and equal-share local cap. Electronic and correction requests feed one retained device ledger; D3 CUDA buffers use its actual allocation/rollback/destruction accounting. Missing inventory symbols and unadmitted CUDA stationary-capacity contexts retain the explicit standalone correction owner. This does not provide D4/gCP global planning, general DF-KS inventories, complete vendor memory, or resource authority for every method.

The bounded two-stage HF execution schedule uses the selected native callback controller: stage order, source-success projection, target-success/convergence density export, reverse-order cleanup and post-cleanup audit scheduling. For all-electron CPU RHF/UHF Direct/DF, the physical fixed-density audit uses one native scope for preparation, Fock/overlap, shared residual reduction and cleanup. The selected native final-verification policy owns scalar target/physical/precision/accuracy/work-budget disposition. Python retains typed planning, resource preflight, audit transport/presentation, typed identity/observable validation and diagnostic presentation, with explicit old-protocol/out-of-range-integer compatibility; unsupported audit domains and missing protocols retain explicit compatibility, never a retry after admitted native refusal; general coarse-to-fine and force-aware physical execution remain Python-owned. Missing-symbol scheduling is explicit compatibility, never a retry after native refusal. Eligible NUM03 forecasting, next-effort hysteresis and measured final gates use shared native metadata decisions; fitting, provenance and custom types remain explicit Python work. Plain-policy occupied-basis projection and pure-density reconstruction share the existing native transport and ordinary CPU eigen provider; old-protocol/custom/unbounded policy domains retain explicit compatibility. Numeric working-capacity admission is not full physical/provider memory authority or target convergence.

Admitted all-electron CPU HF system projection owns overlap preparation and every spin projection natively. Python retains per-item eligibility, immutable source transport, reports and transactional seed installation. Old/custom/unsupported domains retain explicit preparation compatibility; native execution failure never retries it. The composed capacity remains a numeric-matrix envelope rather than complete memory authority.
The native final-state token is authoritative, but cross-endpoint grid/AO cache lifetimes and task schedules still have Python owners.

Exact bundled snapshots prefer the byte-counted, checksum-bound native catalog query/constructor; selected native refusals never retry an older ABI or Python. Capacity and expansion use the same general-template owner, not a second flat catalog. Other admitted BasisSet inputs use element-local FP64 templates; Python, CLI and SDK share native atom/general-contraction expansion and scalar ECP channel mapping. Typed arrays do not authenticate canonical provenance. Python retains native-free preflight/provenance metadata and explicit old-library, Shell and correlation-auxiliary descriptor adapters. Built-in Calculator construction still imports compiler MethodIR/model resolution and owns alias/composition preflight; native method-name/capability lookup stays on the already-selected Calculator library rather than public cached/default-library discovery. The CLI and Python KS wire lowering now share one library-owned build-time catalog: complete matching MethodIR identities and numerical domains borrow native scientific component/exchange arrays while caller execution controls remain unchanged. Same-name custom graphs, noncatalog/unrepresented domains and missing-symbol/library-free metadata retain explicit compiler lowering; actual native refusal never retries it. Custom MethodIR remains explicit compiler work. Complete frontend/SDK/CLI model resolution remains a separate gap.
Correction kernels have native owners; composition, nonlocal source schedules and complete derivative publication must still be audited per method/property. No blanket second-order qualification.

Exact native named FP64 D3 programs also own global-resource-plan execution where the existing electronic planner admits the context. The frontend copies completed correction receipts; selected preparation failures never retry external correction execution. Unqualified force contexts and older libraries retain compatibility. General nonlocal/second-order schedules remain separately tracked.
Keep older-library Hcore and separately qualified stationary-force behavior until native per-prepared admission is positively available.

Missing prepared-resource symbols select the older Python observation/binding adapter. A partial ABI or a refused native create/prepare never retries unbudgeted preparation; frontend handle closure cannot detach an admitted native owner.
